method: For each fixed historic commodity keyword group, count exact matching Hostplant Genus in source-pinned original HOSTS and unique focal 239 butterfly names. Do not assign commodity to exact Latin species. Do not infer port presence or feasible propagule from names.
limits: Positive HOSTS genus overlap is only a possible taxonomic overlap between a commodity genus and a larval-host genus in a modern database, not the species shipped on a particular original voyage.
Historic plant commodities can be processed or non-viable; no dispersal/plant establishment/actual butterfly feeding evidence.
Some genus names have changed or are synonyms; exact source spellings chosen to prevent aggressive false positive matching.
The 239 focal butterfly genus-level inventory is a globally pooled host list, not an island and historical period-specific larval record.
A positive category on a historical pair does not imply that any focal butterfly or host species was transported during that voyage.
